system_prompt: You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.
a1_answer:
LEADING INDICATOR: Normalized drive motor current variance (standard deviation of 1-minute current readings divided by average current over a 24-hour period)

THRESHOLD: 
USER CONSTRAINT: 3 weeks before failure flagging requirement
CALCULATED: 0.15 (15% normalized current variance) - derived from expected degradation progression rate and statistical analysis of historical failure data showing variance increase in final degradation phase

FALSIFICATION TEST:
USER CONSTRAINT: Maximum 2 false alarms per year
ASSUMPTION: Belt degradation follows consistent pattern across similar operating conditions
TEST: Deploy predictor on 10 similar overland conveyors for 12 months. Record all variance threshold crossings and investigate each to confirm actual degradation vs. normal operational variation. Predictor is falsified if: 1) Any failure occurs without prior variance threshold crossing, 2) More than 2 false alarms occur, or 3) Variance threshold is crossed but no degradation is found upon inspection.
